body:
## Pull request overview

This PR upgrades the ObjectGrid/list-view experience to render business-friendly values (currency, percent, dates), apply column alignment in the underlying DataTable DOM, and provide a Storybook demo that exercises the formatting.

**Changes:**
- Enhanced `@object-ui/fields` cell renderers for number/currency/percent formatting, including a percent progress bar and muted placeholders.
- Wired `TableColumn.align` through to `<TableHead>` and `<TableCell>` styling in the complex DataTable renderer.
- Improved `ObjectGrid` column generation with default empty-value handling and auto right-alignment for numeric-like column types; added a “CRM Deals Pipeline” story.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 4 out of 4 changed files in this pull request and generated 8 comments.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx | Adds empty-value placeholder rendering and auto-infers `align: 'right'` for numeric-like column types. |
| packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.stories.tsx | Adds a CRM-style demo story to showcase formatting/alignment behavior. |
| packages/fields/src/index.tsx | Updates percent/number/currency formatting and introduces a percent mini progress bar. |
| packages/components/src/renderers/complex/data-table.tsx | Applies `align` to header/cell DOM classes via `cn()` to support proper column alignment. |

`PercentCellRenderer` only checks `value == null` before `Number(value)`. This makes `''` render as `0%` and invalid inputs render `NaN%`, and also sets `aria-valuenow`/bar width to `NaN`. Add `value === ''` and `Number.isNaN(numValue)` handling so empty/invalid values render the placeholder instead of misleading numbers.

Typed columns pass a synthetic field object `{ name, type }` into cell renderers, which drops important metadata (e.g. select options/colors, currency code, precision). If `objectSchema?.fields?.[col.field]` is available, prefer passing that metadata through (optionally overriding `type` from the column) so renderers can format correctly.

New auto-inferred `align` behavior (numeric types default to right alignment) isn’t covered by the existing `ListColumnExtensions.test.tsx` suite. Adding assertions for `align` passthrough/inference would prevent regressions (including explicit overrides like `align: 'left'`).

For `col.align === 'center'`, the header’s inner flex container still uses `justify-between`, so the label won’t actually be centered (text-align doesn’t center a flex item). Consider handling the center case explicitly (e.g. `justify-center`) to make `align: 'center'` behave as expected.
```suggestion
                      col.align === 'right'
                        ? 'justify-end'
                        : col.align === 'center'
                          ? 'justify-center'
                          : 'justify-between'
```

Alignment wiring in `DataTableRenderer` (`text-right`/`text-center` on header + cells) is new behavior and currently untested. Consider extending the existing data-table test suite to assert the correct classes are applied when a column sets `align`.

`NumberCellRenderer` only applies `Intl.NumberFormat` when `typeof value === 'number'`. If numeric values arrive as strings (e.g. from JSON/DB adapters), they’ll skip formatting and lose separators. Consider coercing numeric strings to numbers (and falling back to the placeholder for NaN).

`CurrencyCellRenderer` treats empty string / non-numeric inputs as numbers via `Number(value)`, which turns `''` into 0 and invalid values into `NaN` (rendering `$0.00`/`$NaN`). If empty values should render as a placeholder, add an explicit `value === ''` / `Number.isNaN(...)` check before formatting.
